title: An array<int, scalar> argument cannot satisfy a parameter declared array<string>

ground_truth.statement: PHP does not enforce a docblock element type, so an array that the caller declares array<int, scalar> may hold a float. The callee declares array<string> and passes every element to strlen(), and under strict_types that call fails with a TypeError on the float. Passing an argument of type array<int, scalar> into a parameter of type array<string> is therefore unsound: the parameter's declared element type is a contract the argument cannot meet, and a diagnostic belongs on the call.

notes: The rule under test is the value dimension of an array argument's type: a parameter declared array<string> promises its elements are strings, and an argument declared array<int, scalar> may hold a float or a bool instead. The runtime script is the neutral ground truth for all three tools: it shows the argument really carrying a non-string element, and it shows the callee failing on it, so the report is required rather than optional and neither PHPStan's argument.type nor Psalm's ArgumentTypeCoercion nor Mago's possibly-invalid-argument is a defect here. This is a regression guard: all three pinned versions report the call (PHPStan 2.3.1, Psalm 6.20.0, Mago 1.57.0), so it documents a green row rather than a divergence. The lead was catalogue candidate psalm:0ee15c8f34d3836c9539 (Psalm's tests/ArgTest.php:186, allowArrayScalarForArrayStringWithArgumentTypeCoercionIgnored); the fixture is a clean-room minimal rewrite, not a copy of the test body, and no tool is judged against that suite here - all three expectations follow from the runtime proof. Psalm's upstream fixture suppresses ArgumentTypeCoercion with an annotation, which is consistent with the expectation recorded here: by default Psalm emits the coercion as an error.

sources.note: lead only; the declared element type array<string> of the parameter is the part that is kept, the rule was re-derived from the runtime
